abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge, and scientific RAG has emerged as a distinct research frontier. Yet no survey treats it as a field in its own right. Existing reviews subsume it under general-purpose RAG and organize systems by retriever-generator pipelines, overlooking what sets scientific practice apart: what knowledge a system draws upon and what operation it performs on that knowledge. We present the first comprehensive survey of scientific RAG, using a 331-paper catalog to organize the field around the pipeline a system runs. The knowledge it retrieves is a substrate, namely Textual, Relational, Structured-entity, or Perceptual, whose native form fixes the matching operation it admits. The task it serves fixes the ground truth that scores its output, and rises by how far that truth sits from the corpus, from grounding through synthesis to discovery. The method connecting them specializes each stage, up to how deeply a verifier couples into generation. Across the catalog, a field's maturity tracks whether its knowledge can be made retrievable and its outputs verifiable. We close with a research agenda spanning adapting general RAG capabilities, building the components the field still lacks, and confronting the limits set by tacit and access-restricted knowledge.

K.intro: The form in which a source stores its knowledge determines what can be retrieved from it. Text can be reached by text, but much of science is not text: a molecule, a graph of typed relations, or a raw instrument signal shares no words with a query, so none of them can be searched the way a passage is. Because a source's native form dictates whether a query can reach it at all, we organize knowledge sources by that form into four retrieval substrates, Textual, Relational, Structured-entity, and Perceptual, and describe what each one stores. Table catalogs representative resources under each substrate.
K.summary: The form in which a source stores its knowledge determines what can be retrieved from it.

substrates.name: Textual
substrates.intro: The textual substrate is the prose record of science, the papers, abstracts, clinical notes, and guideline documents in which findings are written down. It is the largest and most accessible of the scientific data types, and the only one already cast in the natural language a query is posed in.
substrates.summary: The textual substrate is the prose record of science, the papers, abstracts, clinical notes, and guideline documents in which findings are written down.

subsubs.title: General-purpose and domain literature
subsubs.text: General-purpose corpora carry no disciplinary boundary, so a single pipeline serves many fields. Crossref is the registry of DOIs and their publication metadata, and ORCID the companion registry of author identities. OpenAlex aggregates these with PubMed and repository records into an open index of works, authors, venues, institutions, and concepts. S2ORC adds parsed full text in a unified citation-linked space, while Scopus, Web of Science, and Dimensions provide abstract-and-citation metadata and CORE aggregates open-access full text, under varying access terms. Domain indices serve one field with richer metadata. PubMed indexes biomedical abstracts under the MeSH vocabulary, Europe PMC adds open full text, and Embase covers the pharmacology literature commercially. NASA ADS covers astronomy, INSPIRE-HEP high-energy physics, and GeoRef the geosciences, while the IPCC assessment reports form a canonical climate-synthesis corpus. These are also repackaged into ready-made retrieval corpora: MedCorp combines PubMed, StatPearls, textbooks, and Wikipedia, MatSciKB does the same for materials science, and PMC Open Access supplies open full text.
subsubs.summary: General-purpose corpora carry no disciplinary boundary, so a single pipeline serves many fields.

resources.name: Crossref
resources.desc: Registry of DOIs and publication metadata.

resources.name: OpenAlex
resources.desc: Open index of works, authors, venues, and concepts.

resources.name: S2ORC
resources.desc: Parsed full text in a citation-linked space.

resources.name: MedCorp
resources.desc: Ready-made medical RAG corpus (PubMed, StatPearls, textbooks, Wikipedia).

resources.name: PMC Open Access
resources.desc: Open-access full-text subset of PubMed Central.

subsubs.title: Preprint literature
subsubs.text: Preprints trade peer review for recency, offering the most current view of active science. arXiv is the multidisciplinary anchor over a public OAI-PMH interface and bulk S3 access, with author-assigned subject categories. Field servers complement it where arXiv's coverage is limited, including bioRxiv, medRxiv, ChemRxiv, EarthArXiv, and OSF Preprints.
subsubs.summary: Preprints trade peer review for recency, offering the most current view of active science.

subsubs.title: Institution-private corpora
subsubs.text: Institution-private corpora are collaboration wikis, logbooks, and internal notes that share the same textual substrate but stay behind access restrictions. On-premise systems retrieve over them while keeping the data private, as in MITRA over CMS collaboration documentation and DUNE-GPT over Fermilab's internal resources.
subsubs.summary: Institution-private corpora are collaboration wikis, logbooks, and internal notes that share the same textual substrate but stay behind access restrictions.

resources.name: MITRA
resources.desc: On-premise RAG over CMS collaboration documentation (system).

resources.name: DUNE-GPT
resources.desc: RAG over Fermilab DUNE internal resources (system).

substrates.name: Relational
substrates.intro: The relational substrate is the curated web of scientific relations, the graphs that record how genes, diseases, drugs, and concepts connect. Its knowledge lives not in any single node but in the edges between them, the asserted links that no one document states in one place.
substrates.summary: The relational substrate is the curated web of scientific relations, the graphs that record how genes, diseases, drugs, and concepts connect.

subsubs.title: Curated concept-relation graphs
subsubs.text: These are expert-curated graphs of asserted relations among canonical scientific entities. UMLS unifies biomedical vocabularies, while SNOMED CT and ICD-10/11 supply clinical and diagnostic terms. PrimeKG and DRKG assemble integrated drug, disease, and target relations, while STITCH records chemical-protein interactions. STRING protein-interaction data, KEGG, Reactome, and Gene Ontology map pathways and functional annotation, and the disease-gene resources OMIM, DisGeNET, and ClinVar link variants to phenotypes.
subsubs.summary: These are expert-curated graphs of asserted relations among canonical scientific entities.

subsubs.title: Literature-derived graphs
subsubs.text: The same primary literature, once its citations and shared entities are linked, forms a graph rather than a set of passages. OpenCitations and the citation layers of OpenAlex and S2ORC expose reference edges between papers, over which task-specific graphs of papers and their extracted concepts are built.
subsubs.summary: The same primary literature, once its citations and shared entities are linked, forms a graph rather than a set of passages.

resources.name: OpenAlex
resources.desc: Open index of works, authors, venues, and concepts.

resources.name: S2ORC
resources.desc: Parsed full text in a citation-linked space.

resources.name: OpenCitations
resources.desc: Open citation index over the literature.

substrates.name: Structured-entity
substrates.intro: The structured-entity substrate is the objects of science themselves, the molecules, crystals, and materials held as data rather than described in words. Carrying no text, they can be reached only in their own terms, by matching a structure or a target property.
substrates.summary: The structured-entity substrate is the objects of science themselves, the molecules, crystals, and materials held as data rather than described in words.

subsubs.title: Molecule and structure libraries
subsubs.text: These are libraries of molecular and 3D structure. The molecule libraries ChEMBL, ZINC, and PubChem hold compound records, and the 3D structure archives PDB, AlphaFold DB, and CrossDocked2020 hold atomic coordinates. A 2D fingerprint cannot capture 3D shape and a SMILES string drops stereochemistry, so the geometry that governs binding survives only in the 3D-coordinate form.
subsubs.summary: These are libraries of molecular and 3D structure.

subsubs.title: Property databases
subsubs.text: These are property tables built from large-scale computation or measurement. Materials Project, OQMD, AFLOW, and Open Catalyst provide DFT-computed materials properties, QM9 and QMugs provide molecular properties, and BindingDB provides measured binding affinities.
subsubs.summary: These are property tables built from large-scale computation or measurement.

substrates.name: Perceptual
substrates.intro: The perceptual substrate is the raw output of scientific instruments, the images, spectra, and signals recorded straight from measurement. They carry no words at all, so nothing can be retrieved from them until an encoder is learned to connect a signal to a text query.
substrates.summary: The perceptual substrate is the raw output of scientific instruments, the images, spectra, and signals recorded straight from measurement.

subsubs.title: Medical and biological imaging
subsubs.text: Medical imaging dominates this modality. MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray pair chest X-rays with radiology reports, and pathology and ophthalmology corpora extend the setting. The neuroimaging cohorts ADNI, OASIS, and ABIDE, together with the histopathology atlases TCGA (via the Cancer Imaging Archive) and the Human Protein Atlas, provide further imaging substrates.
subsubs.summary: Medical imaging dominates this modality.

subsubs.title: Spectral libraries
subsubs.text: Spectral libraries store the raw signal traces that identify a molecule. Mass-spectral libraries such as MassBank and GNPS, together with the spectral layers of HMDB, are the entry point for de novo structure elucidation from raw spectra.
subsubs.summary: Spectral libraries store the raw signal traces that identify a molecule.

subsubs.title: Instrument arrays and time series
subsubs.text: Arrays and time series are the numerical readings streamed from instruments, and no standard encoder for them exists yet. Sky-survey archives (SDSS, Gaia, MAST ), earth-observation grids (NASA EOSDIS, CMIP6, NOAA NCEI, USGS EROS ), physiological ECG traces, and the collision records of CERN Open Data are among the largest open archives in science, yet almost none are indexed as a retrieval corpus by any cataloged scientific RAG system.
subsubs.summary: Arrays and time series are the numerical readings streamed from instruments, and no standard encoder for them exists yet.

O.intro: A system's operational objective is the task it must serve, and each such task is operationalized by a benchmark that fixes the query, corpus, and ground truth of the pipeline equation. What output the task demands sets all three: some answers lie ready in the corpus as a stored label, others are proposals it does not contain that only an external verifier can judge. We order the seven task families of scientific RAG, from question answering to hypothesis generation, by this distance from the corpus, and Table lists each with its scale and substrate.
O.summary: A system's operational objective is the task it must serve, and each such task is operationalized by a benchmark that fixes the query, corpus, and ground truth of the pipeline equation.

tasks.name: Question Answering
tasks.text: Question answering poses a question with a determinate answer and scores the returned answer against a gold label. Text-only benchmarks cover clinical and biomedical questions in MIRAGE, a suite of five medical QA sets, and PubMedQA, yes/no/maybe questions over abstracts, with LitQA2 requiring answers found only in paper bodies. Broader science is covered by MaScQA for materials-exam problems scored against official answer keys and SciQ for crowd-sourced multiple-choice questions across biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics. Retrieval over a Relational source appears in SciQA, which answers SPARQL queries over the Open Research Knowledge Graph against a gold answer set. Cross-modal question answering pairs a question with non-text evidence over the Perceptual substrate, as in the pathology-image benchmarks PathMMU and Path-VQA. Question answering is the most saturated task in scientific RAG, because its gold labels make scoring automatic, but that same fixed gold cannot separate genuine retrieval from parametric recall, and overlap between corpus and benchmark inflates the reported score.
tasks.summary: Question answering poses a question with a determinate answer and scores the returned answer against a gold label.

tasks.name: Claim Verification
tasks.text: Claim verification presents a claim and scores a verdict of supported, refuted, or unverifiable, reconciled across the retrieved evidence over the Textual substrate. SciFact judges claims against abstracts over a small curated corpus, SciFactOpen extends verification to open-domain retrieval over a pool of half a million documents, and ContraCrow scales it to whole-paper contradiction detection validated against expert judgment. These benchmarks certify correct verdicts on a closed claim set, but the sharp performance drop from SciFact to SciFact-Open shows that they do not measure generalization to novel claims outside it.
tasks.summary: Claim verification presents a claim and scores a verdict of supported, refuted, or unverifiable, reconciled across the retrieved evidence over the Textual substrate.

tasks.name: Literature Synthesis
tasks.text: Literature synthesis poses a question whose answer no single source states and scores the integration across many sources. Long-form aggregation is scored for multi-paper coverage and citation support in ScholarQABench, for abstractive review summarization in PubMedRS-200, and for paragraph summaries in the ideal-answer track of BioASQ, with SQuAI judging answers directly against the evidence they cite rather than a reference text. These benchmarks retrieve over the Textual substrate, and synthesis that follows citation links extends to the Relational substrate in Multi-XScience, which generates a related-work paragraph from a paper and the abstracts of its references. Synthesis benchmarks measure whether an answer is citation-supported and covers a reference answer, but coverage is scored against a fixed expert reference rather than the full relevant literature, so completeness is only partially certified.
tasks.summary: Literature synthesis poses a question whose answer no single source states and scores the integration across many sources.

tasks.name: Property Prediction
tasks.text: Property prediction specifies an entity and a target property and scores the prediction against a held-out measurement. Curated-database recovery over the Structured-entity substrate covers molecular property and toxicity in MoleculeNet and the Therapeutics Data Commons, and protein function against time-delayed annotations in CAFA. Measured-response recovery covers gene-perturbation response in GEARS and PerturBench. Link prediction over the Relational substrate scores held-out biomedical edges in OpenBioLink and OGB-biokg, and spectrum-to-molecule elucidation over the Perceptual substrate scores recovered structures in MassSpecGym. A held-out reference contains only what has already been measured, so a correct prediction outside it is scored as wrong, and recovery certifies fit rather than mechanism, since a strong fit can be interpolation.
tasks.summary: Property prediction specifies an entity and a target property and scores the prediction against a held-out measurement.

tasks.name: Molecular Design
tasks.text: Molecular design sets a target such as a protein pocket or a property profile and scores a proposed molecule the corpus does not contain. PMO defines a set of property-optimization objectives under a capped oracle-call budget, and CrossDocked2020 provides docking pockets against which a generated ligand and its 3D pose are scored for structural accuracy. These benchmarks retrieve over the Structured-entity substrate for molecular structure and over the Perceptual substrate when a 3D pose conditions generation. Design benchmarks score binding or property proxies computed in silico, so a high score certifies the proxy rather than the wet-lab outcome it stands for.
tasks.summary: Molecular design sets a target such as a protein pocket or a property profile and scores a proposed molecule the corpus does not contain.

tasks.name: Materials Discovery
tasks.text: Materials discovery sets a design target such as a stable crystal or a catalytic surface and scores it by re-running a physics simulator over the Structured-entity substrate of crystal and surface records. Matbench Discovery scores thermodynamic stability against DFT-relaxed ground truth, ADsorbML re-evaluates each adsorption structure with a DFT single point, MLIP Arena tests dynamical consistency beyond static references, and ScienceAgentBench executes generated code against task success criteria. A simulator confirms candidates far faster than laboratory screening, but it cannot judge the limits of its own functionals, kinetics, or synthesis feasibility, bounding what a passing score establishes.
tasks.summary: Materials discovery sets a design target such as a stable crystal or a catalytic surface and scores it by re-running a physics simulator over the Structured-entity substrate of crystal and surface records.

tasks.name: Hypothesis Generation
tasks.text: Hypothesis generation provides a research context and scores a proposed idea, mechanism, or pathway that has no stored answer to match, recovering it against a held-out reference rather than a lexical gold. Rediscovery benchmarks withhold findings published after a model's knowledge cutoff and score how closely a generated hypothesis matches the withheld one, MOOSE-Chem scoring chemistry hypotheses against expert-annotated 2024 papers and ResearchBench decomposing discovery into inspiration retrieval, hypothesis composition, and ranking a gold hypothesis above generated negatives across twelve disciplines. HypoBench measures the recovery rate of ground-truth patterns on synthetic tasks, and TruthHypo scores the groundedness of biomedical hypotheses against a knowledge graph and a domain-specific corpus over the Relational substrate. These benchmarks retrieve inspirations over the Textual substrate of prior literature and, in TruthHypo, over a Relational knowledge graph. Because their verifier is a similarity match to a held-out finding or a groundedness check rather than a physical simulator, hypothesis generation sits at the weakest verification of the seven tasks, though contamination-controlled rediscovery makes its scores more reproducible than open-ended novelty rating.
tasks.summary: Hypothesis generation provides a research context and scores a proposed idea, mechanism, or pathway that has no stored answer to match, recovering it against a held-out reference rather than a lexical gold.

M.intro:
A scientific RAG system solves the tasks of the Operational Objective axis by turning a query into an output through the pipeline of the overview figure, and we organize its methods by the stage at which they act. Given a query and a knowledge source already compiled into one of the substrates of the Knowledge Source axis, the pipeline unfolds the retrieval of the pipeline equation into its parts and wraps it in a loop that drafts an output, checks it, and refines it,

^(t) =_generator!(q, ! (R^(t))_reranker, (^(t-1))_verifier),

R^(t) =*sel_u; s(((q,^(t-1)))_transformed, encoded query, (u)_indexed key),

Here rewrites the query, optionally folding in the current draft, encodes the rewritten query into the space of the keys that built at construction, and the substrate-bound score matches the two. reranks what retrieval returns, generates the output from the query, the evidence, and any feedback, and tests that output against a signal from beyond the corpus. The loop runs for from an empty draft, so a system that never checks its output runs a single pass, while one that refines against a verifier repeats. The final is scored by against the benchmark's ground truth.

The four stages follow in turn, each organized by substrate. Construction starts from a knowledge source of the Knowledge Source axis and encodes each of its units with into the searchable index, in the form its substrate dictates. Retrieval matches a query against that index through the transform, the encoding, and the substrate-bound score, returning a set of units. Integration reranks those units with and generates the output with. Verification tests that output with a verifier at depth. Tablethe systems table groups representative systems by the depth of verifier coupling they reach, from open generation to closed-loop refinement.
M.summary: A scientific RAG system solves the tasks of the Operational Objective axis by turning a query into an output through the pipeline of the overview figure, and we organize its methods by the stage at which they act.

stages.name: Knowledge Construction and Indexing
stages.intro: Construction is the offline step that builds the index. It runs each unit of a knowledge source through an encoder that turns the unit into a searchable key, a passage into a dense vector, a molecule into a structural fingerprint, a raw signal into an embedding. Because this key takes a different form on each substrate, the rest of this section builds the index one substrate at a time.
stages.summary: Construction is the offline step that builds the index.

subsubs.title: Passage indexing of textual sources
subsubs.text: Over the textual substrate, a unit and a query are both text, so is one text encoder shared between them, embedding each passage into a dense vector matched by similarity or indexing it as sparse lexical terms matched by word overlap. Systems differ mainly in that encoder and the corpus they run it over. MEDRAG builds sparse and dense indexes over a mixed medical corpus of tens of millions of snippets, BioRAG trains a PubMedBERT-based domain embedding over 22 million life-science abstracts, and HiPerRAG parses 3.6 million articles and indexes them with a contrastively fine-tuned dense encoder. The same construction extends to institution-private corpora that never leave the premises. MITRA scrapes and runs OCR on CMS analysis notes into an on-premise dense index, and the multi-facility framework of Sulc et al. builds per-facility indexes over accelerator logbooks. DUNE-GPT, the RHIC preservation assistant, AccGPT, and a tokamak-log copilot index the internal documentation of their collaborations, keeping the stack local to preserve closed data. Because passages are chunked, the recurring failure is the loss of context that spans chunk boundaries. A passage index serves Question Answering and Literature Synthesis.
subsubs.summary: Over the textual substrate, a unit and a query are both text, so is one text encoder shared between them, embedding each passage into a dense vector matched by similarity or indexing it as sparse lexical terms matched by word overlap.

subsubs.title: Graph construction from relational sources
subsubs.text: Over the relational substrate, the unit of retrieval is a subgraph, so has two parts, embedding each node's text label so a query can locate an entry node while keeping the graph structure itself as the index to traverse from there. Construction therefore extracts entities and typed relations and reconciles them to shared identifiers. KG-RAG links query entities to nodes of the SPOKE biomedical graph, MedGraphRAG uses a large language model to build a three-tier graph over patient documents, literature, and the UMLS vocabulary, and CG-RAG builds a chunk-level citation graph that links passages by intra-document and citation edges. The graph keeps every grounded or synthesized claim traceable through typed edges, but its recurring failure is the flattening of edge weights and relation semantics when a retrieved subgraph is verbalized for the generator.
subsubs.summary: Over the relational substrate, the unit of retrieval is a subgraph, so has two parts, embedding each node's text label so a query can locate an entry node while keeping the graph structure itself as the index to traverse from there.

subsubs.title: Structure indexing of structured-entity sources
subsubs.text: Over the structured-entity substrate, an object carries no text to embed, so encodes it in its own form, a fingerprint, a descriptor, or a learned graph encoder for its structure, or a table of computed or measured values when retrieval is by property. Systems differ in the representation they choose and how they organize it. f-RAG slices molecules into a fragment vocabulary ranked by molecular property, and Rag2Mol builds a molecular library specific to each target protein pocket. MMPT-RAG indexes a large database of matched molecular pair transformations mined from chemical and patent corpora, and RADiAnce builds a contrastive latent space over known protein interfaces so that binders can be retrieved across domains. Because proximity in a structural representation need not mean proximity in the property of interest, the recurring failure is the gap between structural and property space. A structure index makes Molecular Design and Materials Discovery reachable, since a novel candidate is assembled from indexed structures.
subsubs.summary: Over the structured-entity substrate, an object carries no text to embed, so encodes it in its own form, a fingerprint, a descriptor, or a learned graph encoder for its structure, or a table of computed or measured values when retrieval is by property.

subsubs.title: Cross-modal encoding of perceptual sources
subsubs.text:
Over the perceptual substrate, no encoder exists before construction, so and the query encoder must be trained together into one shared space, over the signal and over text, so that an inner product can later match them. This makes construction the heaviest of the four substrates, since without that alignment there is no index at all. MMed-RAG trains domain-specific image-report retrievers for radiology, ophthalmology, and pathology, FactMM-RAG trains a report retriever on factual image-report pairs mined with RadGraph, LaB-RAG predicts categorical labels on top of frozen image embeddings to filter which report examples are retrieved, MADGEN aligns a tandem mass spectrum with molecular scaffolds by contrastive learning, and CardioRAG encodes a twelve-lead electrocardiogram with a variational autoencoder. Because the shared space separates signals only along the axes its training pairs distinguished, the recurring failure is that any signal detail never named in the paired text is invisible to retrieval.

The construction choice fixes what a system can later search and which objective it can pursue. The same molecule is reachable by its structure only if it was fingerprinted at construction, and remains reachable only as text if it was stored as a passage.
subsubs.summary: Over the perceptual substrate, no encoder exists before construction, so and the query encoder must be trained together into one shared space, over the signal and over text, so that an inner product can later match them.

stages.name: Retrieval
stages.intro: Retrieval decides which stored knowledge the system can actually use, since a generator reasons only over what retrieval returns. In science the difficulty is that the query and its target are often not both text. Matching a question to a passage is routine, but matching a spectrum to a molecule or a symptom to a graph node is not, so the matching operation is fixed by the substrate rather than chosen freely. Formally, retrieval builds the set of the pipeline equation through a query transform, a query encoding, and a match score. Of these, only is substrate-bound, matching against the keys that the encoding shaped at construction. The rest of this section covers each substrate's matching operation, together with which store to query and whether to retrieve at all.
stages.summary: Retrieval decides which stored knowledge the system can actually use, since a generator reasons only over what retrieval returns.

subsubs.title: Query transformation
subsubs.text: The text a user submits is often not the best text to search with, so many systems rewrite the query before encoding it, which is the role of the transform. The rewrite may add reasoning, broaden coverage, or break a hard question apart. RAG searches with a generated rationale instead of the bare question, so the retriever sees the reasoning the answer will need. Pathfinder expands the query into a hypothetical answer and searches with that, on the premise that a plausible answer looks like the passages that support it. SQuAI splits a complex question into sub-questions and retrieves for each, and HyKGE emits an intermediate hypothesis to widen its exploration of the graph. BioRAGent expands the query with synonyms and related terms generated from a few examples, so a document that uses different wording is still found. Because it acts on the query alone, this step is independent of the substrate and helps every objective.
subsubs.summary: The text a user submits is often not the best text to search with, so many systems rewrite the query before encoding it, which is the role of the transform.

subsubs.title: Substrate-fixed matching
subsubs.text: Matching is where the substrate asserts itself, because whether a stored item counts as similar to a query depends on what kind of thing that item is. A passage can be compared by its words or its meaning, but a molecule, a graph node, or an image cannot be compared the same way, so each Knowledge Source carries its own matching operation. Over the Textual substrate, matching is similarity between texts, measured either lexically by shared words or densely by shared meaning in an embedding space. MEDRAG runs several such retrievers together, BM25, Contriever, SPECTER, and MedCPT, and merges their rankings by reciprocal rank fusion. Over the Relational substrate the index is a graph, so matching means walking its edges outward from the query entities. KG-RAG takes the immediate neighbors of a node in SPOKE, MindMap follows longer multi-hop paths between two query entities, and GraPPI slides a nearest-neighbor window across the STRING protein graph. Over the Structured-entity substrate, items are matched by their structure rather than by any text describing them. f-RAG retrieves molecular fragments ranked by a target property, and RetMol retrieves whole exemplar molecules that best satisfy the target property. Keying on structure this way is what lets these systems serve Molecular Design. Over the Perceptual substrate the query is a raw signal compared directly to candidates. MMed-RAG sends a query image to a retriever trained for its imaging domain, and PathoAgenticRAG finds page-level pathology-textbook images by joint image-text similarity. When the knowledge instead lives behind a database rather than a local index, matching is not a similarity computation at all but a call to that service. LLaMP lets a reasoning agent query the Materials Project, and GeneGPT writes and runs NCBI web-service calls, each returning an exact value to ground the answer.
subsubs.summary: Matching is where the substrate asserts itself, because whether a stored item counts as similar to a query depends on what kind of thing that item is.

subsubs.title: Source planning and adaptive retrieval
subsubs.text:
Before any of these matches runs, a system may have to make two prior decisions. The first is where to look, when the knowledge is split across several stores of different kinds. Omni-RAG handles this with a small trained planner that routes a medical question to the right member of a five-source knowledge base spanning text and a graph. The second decision, which matters more in science than in general search, is whether to retrieve at all, because pulling in an outdated protocol can be worse than retrieving nothing. Self-BioRAG therefore predicts on demand whether a given query needs retrieval, rather than retrieving for every one.

Scientific retrieval keys on representations that text similarity cannot address. A query given as a structure or a spectrum must be matched by an operation the substrate supports, so dense-vector retrieval alone reaches a passage but not a binding pocket.
subsubs.summary: Before any of these matches runs, a system may have to make two prior decisions.

stages.name: Integration and Generation
stages.intro: Once evidence is retrieved, integration decides how it enters generation, and this is where the reranker and the generator of the pipeline equation act. The form of integration sets how tightly the retrieved evidence governs the output, ranging from loosely conditioning to strictly constraining.
stages.summary: Once evidence is retrieved, integration decides how it enters generation, and this is where the reranker and the generator of the pipeline equation act.

subsubs.title: Reranking and filtering
subsubs.text: Retrieval often returns more than the generator should trust, so the first integration step trims the set for precision, and systems differ in the signal they trim on. Pathfinder reranks its top-ranked passages with a Cohere cross-encoder and discards outliers before answering. KG-Rank first ranks the retrieved UMLS triples by concept similarity with maximal-marginal-relevance for diversity, then reranks the survivors with a MedCPT cross-encoder. RAG trains a small filter that keeps only the snippets predicted to lower the answer's perplexity, discarding topically similar distractors. PaperQA2 replaces raw chunks with LLM-written contextual summaries, each scored for relevance so that only the most useful few enter the prompt. RULE instead calibrates the number of retrieved contexts admitted, using a statistical bound that caps the factuality risk from over-reliance on retrieval.
subsubs.summary: Retrieval often returns more than the generator should trust, so the first integration step trims the set for precision, and systems differ in the signal they trim on.

subsubs.title: Fusion and diffusion conditioning
subsubs.text: Some generators do not read the evidence from a prompt at all, but fold it into their own computation. BioReader injects retrieved neighbors into a T5 encoder-decoder by chunked cross-attention while keeping the retriever frozen, and f-RAG and RetMol fuse retrieved fragments and exemplar molecules, respectively, into a frozen molecular generator through a small trained module. Diffusion generators go further and let retrieved structures steer every denoising step, as IRDiff conditions a three-dimensional diffusion model on target-aware reference ligands and READ modulates each step with a retrieved pocket-matched scaffold. Fusion and conditioning carry Structured-entity and Perceptual evidence into Molecular Design.
subsubs.summary: Some generators do not read the evidence from a prompt at all, but fold it into their own computation.

subsubs.title: Constraint and tool use in the loop
subsubs.text: A plain generator can produce fluent text that violates basic science, so some systems bring in rules or tools while the output is being formed. Two mechanisms appear. The first is constraint injection, where explicit physical rules are supplied to steer the generator away from impossible candidates. A high-entropy-catalyst system feeds stoichiometry and stability rules into the prompt, biasing the model toward physically admissible alloy compositions. The second is in-loop tool use, where the generator pauses to call an external resource and continues from its result. LLaMP drives reasoning agents that query the Materials Project for real property values during generation, and HoneyComb runs a thought-action-observation loop that selects and executes tools from a materials tool hub. In both cases the science actively shapes the output as it forms, rather than sitting passively alongside it as retrieved context.
subsubs.summary: A plain generator can produce fluent text that violates basic science, so some systems bring in rules or tools while the output is being formed.

subsubs.title: Long-form synthesis
subsubs.text:
A further class of generators integrates many retrieved sources into one long-form answer, review, or verdict. OpenScholar writes citation-backed answers over a 45-million-paper index and refines them through a self-feedback loop, and Clinfo.AI produces cited clinical answers by abstractive summarization over live literature. AutoSurvey and SurveyForge draft a full survey from a retrieval-guided outline, LitLLM drafts a related-work section from reranked references, and TrialMind searches and screens clinical trials to feed a human-verified meta-analysis. These generators target Literature Synthesis, whose output integrates sources no single one contains.

Across these mechanisms the integration mode sets how tightly retrieved evidence governs the output. Passage concatenation only conditions generation, whereas constraint injection and in-loop tool execution hold it to a scientific validity the looser modes leave unchecked.
subsubs.summary: A further class of generators integrates many retrieved sources into one long-form answer, review, or verdict.

stages.name: Verification
stages.intro: Generation produces an output, but in science that output is trusted only to the extent it has been checked against something beyond the retrieved evidence. Verification is the stage that performs this check, and systems differ in how deeply the verifier is coupled to generation. This coupling is the depth at which an external verifier of the pipeline equation enters the generation loop, from a system that adds no external check to one that refines against a verifier at every step. This depth tends to bound the highest objective a system can reach, since an output is trusted to the extent it has been verified. We read it as a ladder of four rungs of increasing coupling. In terms of the pipeline equation, the rungs fix the verifier and the depth: open generation runs once with no verifier, self-check keeps internal to the retrieved evidence, external verification applies an outside once, and closed-loop refinement runs an outside for.
stages.summary: Generation produces an output, but in science that output is trusted only to the extent it has been checked against something beyond the retrieved evidence.

subsubs.title: Open generation
subsubs.text: The shallowest coupling is no coupling at all, a system that retrieves and generates once and returns the result unchecked. This is enough whenever the answer already lies inside the retrieved evidence, so the generator has only to report it. MEDRAG and HiPerRAG answer a question straight from the passages they retrieve, GeneGPT grounds each answer in the exact value an NCBI web-service call returns, and MADGEN recovers a molecular structure from a mass spectrum in a single spectrum-conditioned pass. Open generation suffices whenever a gold already fixes the answer, whether a Question Answering label or the held-out structure of spectrum-to-molecule Property Prediction, and stops there, because it asserts nothing a gold cannot already check.
subsubs.summary: The shallowest coupling is no coupling at all, a system that retrieves and generates once and returns the result unchecked.

subsubs.title: Self-check
subsubs.text: A self-checking system reads its own draft before committing to it, but the only thing it consults is the evidence it already retrieved, never the outside world. Self-BioRAG rates the relevance and support of each passage with reflective tokens, and PaperQA enforces that every statement stays faithful to a cited source. Because the check never leaves the retrieved evidence, this rung supports Question Answering and much of Literature Synthesis, yet it cannot establish a claim the evidence does not already contain.
subsubs.summary: A self-checking system reads its own draft before committing to it, but the only thing it consults is the evidence it already retrieved, never the outside world.

subsubs.title: External verification
subsubs.text: An externally verified system sends its finished output to an outside process that scores it once, so the judgment comes from beyond the retrieved evidence. IRDiff scores each generated 3D molecule by docking against the target once, and Rag2Mol screens its generated candidates through docking and drug-likeness filters after generation, neither refining against the result. This outside check is what underwrites docking-scored Molecular Design, where a candidate is confirmed against a target the model was not shown.
subsubs.summary: An externally verified system sends its finished output to an outside process that scores it once, so the judgment comes from beyond the retrieved evidence.

subsubs.title: Closed-loop refinement
subsubs.summary: The deepest coupling runs the verifier inside the generation loop and revises the output against its verdict round after round.

E.intro: How an output can be scored depends on what its answer can be compared against. Formally, an output is scored by the term of the pipeline equation against a ground truth, and where comes from differs across tasks. We therefore organize evaluation by what an output is scored against. Retrieval quality is measured against relevance judgments, independent of the final answer. The other three form a ladder ordered by where the ground truth lives, output correctness against a fixed gold inside the corpus, generation quality against a reference where no single gold exists, and verifier-based scoring against a verifier beyond the corpus. Ordering evaluation this way, rather than by whether a gold answer exists as prior RAG-evaluation surveys do, extends the account to the discovery scientific RAG must reach. One benchmark is scored along several of these dimensions at once. Table pairs each dimension with its metrics and the ceiling it cannot cross.
E.summary: How an output can be scored depends on what its answer can be compared against.

subsections.name: Retrieval quality
subsections.intro: Retrieval can be scored on its own, before any answer is written, by asking whether the units a system fetched hold the evidence a question needs. What makes a unit relevant depends on the substrate. A textual query needs a passage that states the right finding, a structural query needs a molecule with the right scaffold, and a spectral query needs the record whose peaks match, so relevance here is a domain judgment rather than a topical resemblance. Against a set of such judgments, the same information-retrieval metrics score the ranking across all seven tasks. Precision@ and recall@ count the relevant units among the top, mean average precision and normalized discounted cumulative gain reward ranking relevant units higher, and mean reciprocal rank rewards returning the first relevant unit early. A high retrieval score shows the needed evidence was placed within reach, but not that the generator used it, since a system can rank the supporting record first and still answer from parametric memory.
subsections.summary: Retrieval can be scored on its own, before any answer is written, by asking whether the units a system fetched hold the evidence a question needs.

subsections.name: Output correctness
subsections.intro: When a scientific question has one established answer, such as a diagnosis, a measured property, or a curated entity, the output is scored by whether it matches that gold. Correctness is judged in the terms of the field rather than by string overlap. This means accuracy and macro-F1 for multiple-choice and yes/no items, agreement with an official answer key for materials-exam problems, and clinical-entity F1 such as CheXbert or RadGraph that checks whether a generated radiology report names the correct findings and their relations. Beyond question answering, it also scores the fixed-label verdict of claim verification. A fixed gold makes scoring automatic and reproducible, yet in science it is a weak test of grounding. The literature a system retrieves over is finite and already absorbed into the model during pretraining, so a correct answer may be one it memorized rather than one it drew from evidence. Only questions whose answers postdate a model's training cutoff separate reasoning over evidence from recall of an established fact.
subsections.summary: When a scientific question has one established answer, such as a diagnosis, a measured property, or a curated entity, the output is scored by whether it matches that gold.

subsections.name: Generation quality
subsections.intro: When no single paper holds the answer, a system synthesizes one across many studies, and the score turns on the quality of that integration. Because a scientific claim must trace to its evidence, faithfulness and citation precision and recall check whether each statement is backed by the studies it cites, and coverage measures how much of an expert reference the synthesis includes. Where no reference fixes the answer, an LLM-as-judge or an expert supplies the score. These certify that a synthesis is attributable and covers its reference, but not that it reflects how the answer was reached, since a citation can be right while the statement was formed without it, that it is complete against the full literature, or that the LLM judge is free of bias toward its own style.
subsections.summary: When no single paper holds the answer, a system synthesizes one across many studies, and the score turns on the quality of that integration.

subsections.name: Verifier-based scoring
subsections.intro: A discovery task proposes an output the corpus does not contain, so scoring calls an external verifier rather than a stored answer, and these verifiers form their own `ladder of strength'. A physics simulator gives the strongest check, scoring a proposed material by its formation energy above the convex hull against DFT-relaxed ground truth, though that ground truth is a ground-state calculation and cannot say whether the material is kinetically accessible or synthesizable. A docking program is weaker, scoring a molecule by a binding-affinity proxy filtered for drug-likeness, where a pose can rank well while remaining physically invalid. A withheld measurement is weaker still, scoring a prediction by how well it recovers an unseen value through Tanimoto similarity, distributional distance, or Fmax, yet a strong fit can be interpolation rather than mechanism, since deep models for gene-perturbation response do not beat simple linear baselines and a mode-collapsed model still scores well on these distributional metrics. At the weakest rung, where no verifier is decisive, LLM-judges and expert ratings stand in. Each verifier certifies that a novel output survives a test the corpus cannot administer, but only as far as its own proxy reaches. No score at any rung is captured by a single number, which can hide an inability to reject an unanswerable question or to reconcile conflicting evidence. The maturity of a result must therefore be read together with the rung it was scored on, since the same number means a verified fact at one rung and a plausible proposal at another.
subsections.summary: A discovery task proposes an output the corpus does not contain, so scoring calls an external verifier rather than a stored answer, and these verifiers form their own `ladder of strength'.

F.intro:
The preceding sections developed the three parts of a scientific RAG system in isolation, the knowledge it draws on, the problem it solves and the standard that scores it (Sectionsthe Operational Objective axis andthe evaluation axis), and the method that connects them. the overview figure joins them into one map a reader can navigate end to end. Reading left to right, a choice of data substrate leads to the benchmarks posed over it, then to every surveyed method that addresses them, listed as citations, and finally to the evaluation that scores the result. The map doubles as an index into the survey, letting a reader locate the exact systems that fit a given data type and task, and its shape shows where systems cluster on the textual substrate and thin toward non-textual discovery, the pattern the rest of this section explains.

Scientific RAG has built unevenly, and where it has and has not built follows from whether a substrate admits a mature matching operation and a task admits an available verifier. Capability is active where both hold, as in literature grounding and synthesis over the Textual substrate and knowledge-base lookup over the Relational and Structured-entity substrates, all resting on mature retrievers and automatic scoring. It is emerging where a single component lags, as in cross-modal grounding, knowledge-graph synthesis, structure-based discovery under a strong verifier, and private-document retrieval. It is dormant where the verifier, retriever, or substrate does not yet exist, so literature-grounded ideation reports only novelty and expert preference through SciMON, MOOSE-Chem, ResearchAgent, and Chain-of-Ideas, spectrum-to-molecule discovery rests on a single system, and observational and tacit synthesis have no retrievable substrate at all. Capability concentrates on the Textual substrate and thins toward discovery. The gaps behind this thinning fall into three distinct causes that organize this section. Some gaps are already solved in general RAG and only await adaptation to scientific workflows (§). Others have no transferable solution and require components built for scientific demands (§). The rest cannot be closed by better architecture at all, because the knowledge is undocumented or restricted by licensing and law (§). We then close with the broader trajectories toward which these frontiers converge (§). the overview figure arranges the open challenges along these three causes, from the tractable to the structural.
F.summary: The preceding sections developed the three parts of a scientific RAG system in isolation, the knowledge it draws on, the problem it solves and the standard that scores it (Sectionsthe Operational Objective axis andthe evaluation axis), and the method that connects them.

subsubs.title: Adaptive Retrieval for Scientific RAG
subsubs.summary: Adaptive retrieval, the ability to dynamically decide when to retrieve and what to trust, is a proven capability in general RAG that cannot be directly transplanted to scientific workflows.

subsubs.title: Reranking for Scientific RAG
subsubs.summary: Reranking is a well-established mechanism in general RAG to improve precision, yet adapting it to science requires fundamentally redefining its core metric: relevance.

subsubs.title: Benchmark Contamination and Evaluation Protocols
subsubs.summary: Benchmark contamination is a well-studied threat in general language models, yet existing mitigation strategies face fundamental limitations in scientific RAG.

subsubs.title: Evaluating Discovery Beyond Proxies
subsubs.summary: the evaluation axis showed that discovery-oriented tasks are always scored against a stand-in for the truth, whether a docking score for binding, a density-functional calculation for stability, or a held-out measurement for an unknown value.

subsubs.title: Building Retrievable Substrates
subsubs.summary: Constructing retrievable substrates is a foundational prerequisite for scientific RAG, as the domain relies on complex data structures that general systems rarely encounter.

subsubs.title: Representing Scientific Identity Across Modalities
subsubs.summary: Effective retrieval requires systems to recognize the underlying scientific identity of an entity regardless of its surface representation, a capability currently lacking in standard models.

subsubs.title: Verifying and Generating Under Scientific Constraints
subsubs.summary: showed that a system reaches the Discovery objective only when an external verifier is coupled into its loop, yet outside molecular docking such verifiers barely exist.

subsubs.title: Engineering Executable RAG and Error Recovery
subsubs.summary: Transitioning scientific RAG from passive text synthesis to active hypothesis testing demands architectures explicitly engineered for computational execution and iterative error recovery, which together form the deepest, closed-loop rung of the verifier coupling in verification.

subsubs.title: Retrieving Across Substrates
subsubs.summary: construction builds each substrate on its own, and nearly every system in this survey commits to just one.

subsubs.title: Building Verification for Verifier-Free Objectives
subsubs.summary: The verifier-coupling ladder of verification stops short at literature-grounded ideation, where no docking program, simulator, or database can confirm a proposed idea.

subsubs.title: Tacit Knowledge and the Limits of Digitization
subsubs.summary: The effectiveness of scientific RAG is fundamentally bound by tacit knowledge that is never digitized.

subsubs.title: Data Access and Licensing Boundaries
subsubs.summary: Even when scientific knowledge is fully digitized, structural accessibility often blocks retrieval.

subsubs.title: Toward Autonomous AI Scientists
subsubs.summary: Evidence grounding is the foundation on which an autonomous AI scientist must stand, and scientific RAG provides it.

subsubs.title: Toward Industrial and Open-Source Convergence
subsubs.summary: One promising direction is the convergence of scientific RAG with industrial platforms and open-source ecosystems.
